h: Climb first, explore after: Portsmouth tips
p: Portsmouth is one of those cities where you could fill a whole week, so slotting a climbing session in needs a little thought. The good news is it's short and sweet. Plan on a couple of hours for the visit, covering arrival, harness fitting, the safety briefing and your time on the walls.

Before you head over, sort the participation forms. Every climber needs one, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s, and it's far quicker to fill in online. Check the age guidance when you book, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and supervision rules for younger children.

A few on-the-wall tips. Climb with your legs, not just your arms. Look up for your next hold rather than down at the floor. And when it's time for the jumps, take a breath, focus on the target and go. The auto-belay does the rest.
Bring water and comfy clothes, and leave rings and watches at home.

There's plenty more to see. The D-Day Story at Southsea tells the tale of the Normandy landings, and Southsea Castle, built by Henry VIII, is right next door on the seafront. Old Portsmouth has the Round Tower and the Hot Walls, with little artists' studios set into the old fortifications. Clarence Pier is the place for traditional seaside fun, and the ferries and hovercraft to the Isle of Wight make for a cracking day trip if you've got time to spare.
